result.scientific_strategy:
## 285f0407-8cc3-401d-bdcd-2af73de9a61c / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official 6–20 cm, full-angle reach-and-hold distribution. PPO learned strong behavior: the baseline checkpoint-100352 reached 97.0% on the research panel and 98.0% on the task-reference panel, while the transferred full-radius experiment reached 98.0% and 98.5% respectively. These are development measurements, not the official assessment. Broader radius exposure corrected two earlier near-base failures, but persistent negative-angle failures and unchanged research-panel failures leave the remaining cause unresolved.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, rather than training reward or the training success proxy, is the relevant progress signal (`research/evaluations/` and `research/results.jsonl`). Later unchanged training degraded or plateaued around the measured checkpoint, so more steps alone are not established as an improvement. Full-radius training produced the best observed task-reference result, but its selected checkpoint still failed at 9.9 cm/-122.9 degrees, 9.4 cm/-127.9 degrees, and 18.2 cm/-154.8 degrees; the research evaluation retained the same four deterministic failures across its three measured checkpoints (`research/evaluations/`, experiment-2 records). The training logs show changing proxy and reward dynamics but cannot establish the cause of those task failures. Development panels are not the official assessment, and repeated episode identities are not new coverage.

**Open questions:** Whether the residual negative-angle failures are improved by emphasizing that angular sector during training while retaining full-radius and full-angle support remains unresolved. It is also unknown whether the residual behavior instead reflects control or hold stability, and whether any development-panel improvement transfers to the official 200-episode assessment.
